items.title: Lucia Actress Manni L. Perez Issues First Statement Since GTA 6 Launch
items.description: Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6, has issued her first statement since the game came out.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6, has issued her first statement since the game came out.

Perez’s role as Lucia Caminos was confirmed when she was nominated in the Best Performance category for this year’s The Game Awards, a day before GTA 6 launched on November 19. She’s now considered the favorite following the game’s critically acclaimed, record-breaking launch.

Now, a week later, Perez took to social media to thank fans for the reception to GTA 6.

“Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” an Instagram Stories post began.

“Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received.

“I've dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.”

“Happy Holiday's y'all.”

Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's easy to know why — GTA 6 sounds like it was a pretty involved project. Indeed, Lucia isn’t Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, she plays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer.

Meanwhile, Jason actor Dylan Rourke also posted a message of gratitude on Instagram Stories, saying: “Thankful for this wild ride. Gratitude won’t cut it. Make today about the ones you love.”

Manni L. Perez shouldn't be confused with Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista in GTA 6. This week, Manny Perez bought a PS5 just so he could play the game, saying in a video posted to social media: “Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy! Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.”

Other GTA 6 actors who've started to talk about their work on the game include Lexie Shoaibi, who recently spoke out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online, and Cocoteo FM radio host Issa Lopez, who described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game.

Last month, the actors behind GTA 5's Franklin, Michael, and Trevor shared their advice for GTA 6's cast in a bid to ready them for the kind of fame few video game actors achieve.

items.title: Microsoft-Owned GitHub Stuns Followers as It Celebrates AnyPS5 Repo in Now-Deleted Tweet
items.description: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.

“GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub,” the post said, before jumping into celebrating the repo. “Does changing where games run cross a legal line?” the tweet asked.

This is insane https://t.co/mwU6VIy1nI

— MVG (@ModernVintageG) November 26, 2026

There was also an official video attached to the tweet, which highlighted a post from an AnyPS5 coder, via Kotaku. The post in the video said: “We have 3 days until GTA 6 everyone[…]get your agents or deevs[sic] and work.”

While the post could easily be the work of a rogue social media person, the optics aren’t good at all. GTA 6 is only officially available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, so both Sony and Microsoft have benefited greatly from the game's record-breaking launch. To see a the Microsoft-owned GitHub post a message to its followers essentially encouraging potential piracy is remarkable.

IGN has asked for comment, but GitHub obviously realized its mistake — it deleted the tweet, after all — but how it even got approved in the first place is a mystery until the company comments.

Take-Two is currently working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port heats up. This follows Cyberleek's alleged released of the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.

The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scenes uses AI to speed along development. Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS, former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible, due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.

It's also worth noting that there is extra interest in a PC version of GTA 6 because the console versions target 30fps. The PC version, resumably, will run at 60fps or whatever frame rate your rig is capable of.

Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.

Here’s the exchange:

IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?

Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.

IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?

Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected.

During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.

“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.

“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”

Zelnick’s talk about legal activities sparks an obvious question: what can game companies do about AI-assisted reverse engineering? It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

items.title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
items.description: Rockstar has explained why some extra violent weapons like chainsaws and katanas are missing from GTA 6.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6, with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to.

Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie.

But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC.

“As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?”

When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.”

I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage.

That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. There’s a world of possibilities out there.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Rerelease Includes a Scene Cut From Avengers: Doomsday
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day rerelease includes a scene cut from Avengers: Doomsday, according to a new report.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day rerelease includes a scene cut from Avengers: Doomsday, according to a new report.

The New York Times published an article on the potential for the release of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 — dubbed DunesDay by fans — to set box office records, and within it is a tease for the extra footage set to be included in Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s return to theaters.

According to the NYT, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will have a scene cut from Doomsday added to the end of the movie as a bonus. We don’t know what’s in the scene, but it’s meant to serve as an ad for the upcoming MCU film. Spider-Man: Brand New Day made an eye-watering $2.5 billion at the global box office, so I assume you've seen it. If so, has the promise of a new Avengers: Doomsday scene convinced you to double-dip? Let us know in the comments!

What we know for sure is that Rosario Dawson will return as Claire Temple in the rerelease, marking her long-awaited comeback to the MCU.

Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow.

Last week, Dawson revealed a photo of her in costume for her first Marvel appearance in a decade, standing in nurse scrubs next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It's a scene that fans thought they'd never get to see after it was deleted from the final cut of the movie. Now, however, it is being reinstated for the film's extended edition rerelease, entitled Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day, alongside a handful of other moments previously left on the cutting room floor.

It's pretty obvious when this scene will take place, as Dawson's character stands next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man who is wearing a hospital gown and his Spidey mask. Of course, Spider-Man finds himself in hospital towards the end of the movie, and Dawson's return will likely answer fan questions surrounding how the superhero got patched up with no one else discovering his identity. (The answer, surely, is that Dawson takes care of him directly — having been used to keeping numerous superhero identities secret in the past.)

Spider-Man: Brand New Day returns to theaters on December 4, 2026, now with Rosario Dawson and an Avengers: Doomsday cut scene included. Avengers: Doomsday itself launches on December 18. Today, we got our first look at Magneto vs Doom in a new teaser for Avengers: Doomsday.

items.title: Rockstar Games Issues Statement as Union Vote Fails
items.description: The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

The shock result comes following the hugely successful launch of GTA 6, which has set records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

Workers at Rockstar Games voted 25% in favour of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB. The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote overlapped with the closing submissions of the employment tribunal, which ended earlier this month. Judgement is currently pending.

If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union had won the vote, it would have become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry.

The ballot saw 93.2% turnout, with 1,544 employees across Rockstar’s UK sites in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating. 1,163 team members voted against IWGB recognition (75.3%), while 381 voted in favour (24.7%).

In a statement issued to IGN, Rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said the company was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.”

“This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” Kolbe continued. “As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.”

The IWGB insisted that Rockstar workers would keep organizing without a formal union recognition deal after the ballot.

The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union shared the following statement:

“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

“Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

“A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

“The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.”

Kolbe had indicated Rockstar’s willingness to work with staff on union recognition, recently telling Bloomberg: “We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.”

“This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” Kolbe continued. “As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.”

The IWGB insisted that Rockstar workers would keep organizing without a formal union recognition deal after the ballot.

items.title: Rockstar North Chief Was Praying GTA 6's Big Story Reveal Stayed Under Wraps Ahead of Launch
items.description: Rockstar North has explained why it was so important that GTA 6's big early story reveal stayed under wraps before the game came out.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Warning! This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6.

GTA 6’s prologue hides a surprise that somehow managed to stay a secret all the way up to players finding out for themselves. And Rockstar North, it turns out, was praying for it not to leak ahead of launch.

During the game’s opening stretch, the story of how Lucia ends up in a Leonida prison is told. This isn’t the surprising part — ever since GTA 6 Trailer 1 we’ve known she’d end up behind bars at some point — but the person she was at a diner moments before her arrest is. Tomás, a few-month-old baby and son of Lucia and Jason, is left behind by his mother in GTA 6’s first truly shocking reveal.

Given the history of leaks associated with GTA 6, it feels like a minor miracle that Tommy’s existence remained a complete unknown until launch. This was something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was keenly aware of.

“No, we never were going to [reveal it]," he told VGC in an interview that took place just before GTA 6 came out last week. "I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'”

As we’ve written about at IGN, the existence of Tomás in GTA 6 is the key to its whole design. It’s what powers Jason and Lucia’s tale, and encourages the player to strive to make more and more money as those family savings goals get higher and higher. It connects us to the characters, and creates a shared objective between us and them. We aren’t simply committing crime for crime’s sake, but doing so with the prospect of being reunited with their son at the end of it.

You can see why such a powerful and surprising narrative device would want to have been kept under wraps by Rockstar. It’s the first, and by no means the only, shocking revelation of GTA 6, all the more effective when witnessed firsthand.

“We never were going to [reveal it],” Nelson explained. “It’s meant to shock. We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.”

items.title: GTA 6 Players Have Found a Cheeky Method to Quickly Steal ATMs
items.description: Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Warning! Potential spoilers for GTA 6 follow.

Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open (check out IGN's guide to all ATM locations in GTA 6 if you need help finding one).

First, though, you need to be able to deal with marked bills through a fence called Yasmini, otherwise the money inside the ATM is worthless and a dye pack will explode in your face. When I got to snatching ATMs, I thought it was cool, but the juice didn’t seem worth the squeeze.

It’s kinda hard to keep things on the downlow when you’re backing a truck up to an ATM, ripping it out of a wall, and tearing down the street with the thing still attached, hoping it’ll burst open and spill its contents onto the street. And when it finally does break open, you have to shoot the money drawers open to get to the goods inside — all for a payout between $6,000-$10,000.

It wasn’t worth the effort, honestly. But there’s a new trick players have discovered to crack those eggs immediately and move onto the next before the cops even know you’re there. I’ve tried it, and like Todd Howard famously once said: it just works.

How to quickly steal an ATM in GTA 6

Here’s what you do. First, you need a truck or other heavy vehicle with a winch attachment at the back. You reverse up to the ATM like normal, and the winch connects to the machine. Now drive forward until the line is taut.

From there, get out of your vehicle and walk up to the ATM with a C4 charge. Hold down aim, and a prompt to place it on the ATM should show up, allowing you to set it on the front with Circle/B. Or throw it at the front of the machine — whatever works.

Once it’s in place, you want to get back in your car and accelerate hard. When it pulls out of the wall, keep dragging it but immediately press unhook, followed by the same button to detonate your charge. It’s important these two actions happen immediately after each other, because the ATM needs to be moving when the explosion happens or the drawers can stay inside the machine.

Done correctly, you can walk over and scoop up the cash and escape before the cops even arrive at the scene. They’ll still be figuring out what happened while you’re hooking up to the next machine, pulling, and sparking up a Cuban. If you need more C4, there’s a free stash of the stuff in the back of Yasmani’s. You can also top up at any Ammunation.

A Simple Trick for Faster ATM Robberies GTA 6 https://t.co/lo6aWdupew

— LUCKY (@Badboy1B) November 25, 2026

Players have been trying to find ways to make quick money in GTA 6 since launch, but most of them are boring exploits. This, though, I can get onboard with because it’s just playing the game as intended in an efficient way, and it’s great fun to slip in and out without the cops getting a whiff of you.

items.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Director David Fincher Sparks Backlash for 'Wildly Dystopian' Vision of AI-powered Filmmaking
items.description: Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.

Fincher, who directed Seven, Fight Club, and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, has reunited with long-term collaborator Brad Pitt for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which was written by Quentin Tarantino. It is a standalone sequel and spinoff to Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, with Pitt reprising his role as stunt double Cliff Booth.

In a recent interview with Sean Fennessey on The Ringer’s Big Picture podcast, Fincher confirmed that he used AI to sync the best take of a line reading with the best performance take when they didn’t align on camera, in order to speed up production by cutting down the number of takes needed. Essentially, he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production.

“We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said. “So it was freeing, it was the freeing up of… think of this entirely plastically. We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. You know what I mean? Just giving ourselves that freedom to go, ‘what is the best thing on the eye, and then what is the best thing on the ear,’ and f***ing do not worry about how we’re going to get there, because we will figure out a way. And we did, in most cases. I think there’s a couple of shots [that] didn’t quite work, but they’re getting there. By the time it’s on service.”

Fincher added that the actors spent just a handful of days re-recording dialogue. Dialogue replacement was just 5% conventionally done, the rest “all AI.”

But it was his comments made later in the interview, where Fincher described how he sees directing with AI going in the future, that have sparked the most vociferous response.

Here’s the relevant section in full:

“I’m imagining — and what I’ve seen with AI technology — I’m imagining a world in the next year where everything that humans do great, like sculpting, painting, ageing, blowing fake spider’s webs into the corner, smoking up a volume, putting a shaft of light in it, putting a crazy f***ing wig on somebody, doing all their makeup… like, I can imagine a world where — and I don’t think we’re far away — you hire all the same people. And you walk into a set that’s beautifully handcrafted, and you hire all those people, and you shoot the master. You shoot the master 20, 25 times till you get it worked out exactly. And you’re doing surface capture at the exact same time that you’re filming. And then you go in and you sit all the actors in chairs wherever they land, and they perform from the clavicles up, same scene, but you move the crew. The crew’s now moving to the next stage, they’re pre-lighting that, they’re getting that ready.

“So essentially, the filmmaking process is about just shooting the masters. And all of the iteration, the over-shoulders, the close-ups, all that stuff is derived from the material that you do sitting in a chair after everyone leaves.

“And then, the part that seems to provoke such a violent, vitriolic response in people — ‘Oh my God, he made me do it 20 times!’ — it’s like, now I don’t need to do that, because I won’t miss focus in AI. And I will land a stick the dolly shot in AI. And I will be able to make sure that that hair doesn’t cross right in front of your cornea in AI.

“And it’ll still be based on real human beings, and it’ll still be based on real human — the way humans move and how they traverse a set and however they pull up their trousers before they sit down or take their coat off — all that stuff will be there, but people will only have to do it 15 times.”

In the interview, Fennessey then asked: “Does working that way appeal to you?”

“Totally,” Fincher replied.

Fincher’s comments were roundly criticized on social media, where people hit out at not just the heavy use of AI in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, but the prospect of seeing a performance from the likes of Brad Pitt that isn’t real.

“David Lynch: The camera accidentally caught a crew member in the mirror so I incorporated him into the story and ended up with one of the most memorable characters in TV and movie history,” writer and critic David Hering said in a post on social media. “David Fincher: I spent $400m to change the shape of Brad Pitt’s mouth when he says ‘hello.’”

“Any movie that uses even a sliver of AI should be immediately disqualified from awards consideration,” said another person. “Disgusting.”

“Saying, ‘I wanna take an actor’s eye movement from Take 1 with an actors lip movement from Take 3’…that’s not the performance the actor gave on set! You don’t get to create the perfect performance by Frankenstein-ing a ‘perfect version’ of the performance and call it directing,” actor Mike Kalinowski commented.

“I’m not saying Fincher is not an incredible director. But he’s also known for doing an ungodly amount of takes to get exactly what he wants. But you’re when you’re working with actors, it’s never gonna be perfect. That’s what makes it art.”

One person called Fincher’s proposed production process “wildly dystopian,” another “depressing as f**k.” Another quipped: “there is no longer a need for David Fincher.” "Imagine doing 135 takes just to be asked back for an ADR session where the Ben Grokfleck Machine updates your lips," another said.

“Fincher's vision of a largely A.I. production is undeniably bleak but I suspect people would be less perplexed if it was more widely understood (as a friend remarked to me recently) that Fincher's filmmaking process was always more about control than perfection,” writer Brendan Hodges said.

However, there are some that are defending Fincher here, saying his AI vision isn’t a million miles away from the editing process that goes on without AI, where different parts of takes are edited together to create the best scene. The counter to that response is of course that there’s a difference between editing together actual performance from different takes, and using AI to create a performance that was never given.

AI is one of, if not the hottest topics in the entertainment industry, and Hollywood is currently wrestling with maintaining its humanity in the creative process while cutting down costs and raising productivity. Hollywood, like the video game industry, is beset with layoffs as cost-cutting and AI disruption hit hard.

Earlier this month, Star Wars writer Tony Gilroy sounded the alarm over the rising tide of AI slop that he said was a threat to human-made movies. Speaking to Vanity Fair, Gilroy implored movie fans to vote against the spread of AI data centers — and even jokingly suggested that the artificial intelligence-fuelling tech hubs should be blown up.

In September, acclaimed filmmaker Guillermo Del Toro spoke out against AI, saying the “alchemy” of creativity and discovery humans experience when crafting a story or artwork is unachievable by a machine, and that many of the best works are often elevated by "accidents" that happen during the creative process.

And in July, The Odyssey director Christopher Nolan praised the "immediate and harsh" judgment of "AI slop" from younger audiences.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth opened in IMAX theaters on November 25, and hits Netflix on December 23.

items.title: GTA 6 Weather Still Not Varied Even After the Patch? PS5 Players Are Sharing a Method That May Help Rain and Thunderstorms Kick In
items.description: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.

Lack of weather variety was something I noticed myself during the game’s review period, but Rockstar deployed a small fix during that time too. It was hard to tell whether it was working as intended because the weather also grows more stark as you move through the game.

“The weather types change throughout each day, and the overall weather pattern changes per chapter, evolving from generally very good weather in the first chapter to much more changeable and stormy in the last chapter,” said Owen Shepherd, vice president of art: lighting and rendering at Rockstar, when I asked.

“This is analogous to Florida’s weather patterns in winter through to summer autumn. During the first chapters there are pockets of rain but due to the localization of weather it is possible to miss these."

However, it seems like the issue persisted into the live version of the game, blurring the line between thematically appropriate and accurate weather patterns and unintended bug. items.title: Another Modder Uses AI to Make a Multiplayer Mode for The Last of Us Part 2 — Will Sony Shut This One Down, Too?
items.description: Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2, insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down."
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2, insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down."

The Last of Us had a brilliant multiplayer mode, with tense gunfights powered by weapon sway, smart cover, and nail-biting in-round crafting that forced you to dig around in your backpack as bullets whizzed over your bonce.

That’s why so many people were excited when Naughty Dog announced a Factions multiplayer game in the works based on The Last of Us Part 2. Naughty Dog, however, eventually realized that making a live-service game would change the studio forever, and cancelled the project to focus instead on its upcoming sci-fi game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet.

The Last of Us Part 2 made some brilliant tweaks to the combat, allowing for better mobility and deeper stealth. The feel of the weapons, the crunch of the impacts, the audiovisual spectacle of it all was just something else, but we can only experience it in single-player, officially.

It’s no wonder people want to make Factions happen, even without Sony’s approval. And in September, a promising mod made some big strides towards getting multiplayer working in The Last of Us Part 2. As soon as it started to get traction, however, the mod was sent a cease and desist letter from Sony. “Hey everyone, as you all know, the TLOU 2 Multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month,” wrote creator 'Speclizer' at the time.

“Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you’ll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own.”

Now there’s a new mod hoping to avoid the eye of Sauron, and it’s already out. The mod is called Twelve Weeks and was built specifically for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC, using, its creator has admitted, generative AI. Modder 'Kellie' admitted to using Claude code for most of the game's development, and AI was even used to write the lore dumps you can find in the game. The art was, however, made using Blender.

The Last of Us returns with a new online multiplayer mode called TWELVE WEEKS created for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC. This free mod is a work in progress allowing players to experience a new version of the beloved Factions multiplayer with tactical survival gameplay https://t.co/2P8Wv4abQb

— 𝗩𝗢𝗬𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗥𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗘 (@VoyagersRevenge) November 24, 2026

It features reworked levels — Supply Raid and Interrogation for now — with team-based 4v4 combat, new weapons, and character customization. Players can use gadgets like molotovs and smoke bombs, while fighting against other players as the WLF and Seraphites. The mod even adds brutal execution moves. You can grab Twelve Weeks on Nexus Mods.

However, the mod probably won't last long. The modders have attempted to cover their backs with a repository disclaimer that said: "Twelve Weeks is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog. The Last of Us is a trademark of its owners. You need your own legitimately purchased copy of the game (Steam). This repository contains no game files and no assets taken from the game."

Will Sony take action? In a reply to someone on YouTube, Kellie said the previous Factions mod got hit by Sony because it was paywalled. "Mine is released already for free and in open source," they said. "Since people have the source code to the full mod already, there ain't much they can do even if they do shut me down."

While The Last of Us Online was canceled, there are hints that Naughty Dog may be ready to return to the series for The Last of Us 3. And then there is HBO's The Last of Us TV series, which is currently shooting its third (and likely last) season.

items.title: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 Patch 16.0 Goes Live, Expands Vanguard Class, Makes Big Balance Changes, and Much More
items.description: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 still receives significant support two years after launch. We’re now up to patch 16, which makes significant balance changes to the game. Check out the patch notes.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 still receives significant support two years after launch. We’re now up to patch 16.0, which makes significant balance changes to the game.

In terms of new features, we’ve got a major expansion of the Vanguard class’ combat abilities (the Grapnel Launcher can now be used at close range!), the new Revenge status effect (hitting enemies afflicted with Revenge also deals damage to nearby enemies), and Wargear 2.3 (Bulwark can now equip and customize Cloak!).

As for cosmetics, the hotly anticipated Deathwatch Champion Pack is out now as part of the Season Pass. There’s also a Mortifactors Cosmetic Pack. I’ve put the balance changes as part of the patch notes below, if you want to skip to them to see what’s happened to your class.

Also interesting is the note about tech improvements with patch 16. Publisher Focus Entertainment says loading times have improved, which players will welcome. There are also memory optimizations, “minor” performance improvements, and “general” connectivity improvements. Anyone who’s played or is still playing Space Marine 2 will hope these improvements are meaningful.

Focus has said that next year, Space Marine 2 will receive three more updates until its third anniversary. Patch 17, 18 and 19 will offer free content as well as Season Pass 3 content with the cosmetic DLCs. There’s a lot of excitement around Patch 17, which adds a brand-new class, the Apothecary, complete with its signature Absolvor Bolt Pistol. Patch 17 also adds a new Operation and fresh Heroic weapons, and a rework of the Heavy class. A new Imperial Fist Champion Pack and a Cosmetic Pack for the Minotaurs chapter are also on the way.

The Switch 2 version of Space Marine 2, however, is delayed out of 2026 into 2027. “Considering its current polishing needs, we are constrained to pushing the release to 2027,” Focus said.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 update 16 patch notes:

NEW FEATURES

New Feature: Vanguard Class Expansion

The Vanguard class receives a major expansion to its combat capabilities. The Grapnel Launcher can now be used at close range, making the ability more versatile and responsive in the heat of battle. The class perk tree has also undergone significant changes, with numerous perks reworked and repositioned, alongside new key perks designed to improve crowd control and increase effectiveness against groups of enemies. These include a new perk that allows the Grapnel Launcher to apply Stun and Revenge status effects.

New Feature: Revenge Status Effect

Hitting enemies afflicted with Revenge status effect also deals damage to nearby enemies.

🟡Revenge base damage increased by 50%.

🟡Revenge damage radius increased from 10 to 12 meters.

🟡Revenge maximum number of targets increased from 4 to 5 enemies.

🟡Revenge effect duration increased from 8 to 10 seconds.

New Feature: Wargear 2.3

The Bulwark class receives expanded customization options. Robes and tabards can now be customized through a dedicated Wargear slot instead of the Chest slot, offering more freedom to personalize its appearance. Additionally, Bulwark can now equip and customize Cloak.

Chaos Siege Mode Map Expansion: Sector #3

The final part of the "Hive" map. Deep within the hive city of Avarax, the forces of Chaos are preparing a Daemon Host ritual. Loyalists are attempting to put an end to this heresy.

New Heroic Items

Added 6 Heroic Weapons to unlock with Accolades:

  • Bolt Rifle
  • Heavy Bolter
  • Plasma Rifle
  • Heavy Bolt Pistol
  • Las Fusil
  • Omnissian Axe

Added 4 Heroic Armour Parts to unlock with Accolades:

  • Iron Priest Helmet for Techmarine Class
  • Mark VII Hybrid Helmet for all classes
  • Mark VI Hybrid Helmet for all classes
  • Mark VII Gravis Hybrid Helmet for Heavy Class

New Season Pass Content

☠️ Deathwatch Champion Pack

Vanguard Champion + Occulus Bolt Carbine weapon skin

💀 Mortifactors Cosmetic Pack

  • Mark VII Helmet
  • Breastplate
  • L&R Pauldron

​GAMEPLAY AND BALANCING TWEAKS

Firearms in PvE

Inferno Pistol

  • Base damage is increased by 30%.
  • Standard-Issue version:
    • Damage fall off is changed from 45% to 30%.
  • Master-Crafted – Alpha version:
    • Damage fall off distance end point is changed from 7.5 metres to 8 metres.
    • Damage reduction is changed from 45% to 30%.
  • Salvation of Bakka version:
    • Damage fall off distance end point is changed from 8.5 metres to 9 metres.
    • Damage reduction is changed from 45% to 30%.
  • Gathalamor Crusade version:
    • Damage fall off distance start point is changed from 6m to 5m, end point is changed from 9.5 metres to 10 metres.
    • Damage reduction is changed from 45% to 30%.

Melta Rifle (Heroic version)

  • Ammo reserve is changed from 10 to 15 rounds.

Plasma Incinerator / Heavy Plasma Incinerator

  • “Rapid Cooling” perk duration is reduced from 10 seconds to 5 seconds.

Plasma Pistol

  • Added to Vanguard’s Secondary weapons.

Occulus Bolt Carbine

  • Fixed the menu description of the “Able Headshot” perk of the Occulus Bolt Carbine to reflect the correct value (25%).

🟡 Heavy Bolter (Heroic version - Infernus Heavy Bolter)

  • Overheating is reduced by 50% for the Flamethrower.
  • Headshot Multiplier is increased from 1.7 to 1.8.

🟡 Plasma Incinerator (Heroic version)

  • Full overheating duration is increased from 1.6 to 2.6 seconds.

🟡 Las Fusil (Heroic version)

  • Fire rate is increased from 45 to 90 rounds per minute.
  • Magazine capacity is increased by 1 round.
  • Headshot Multiplier is increased from 3.5 to 4.0.
  • Round regeneration time is reduced from 9 to 8 seconds.

Melee in PvE

One Handed Hammer

  • Reworked Charged Impact, Ground Slam and Energised Strike attacks, to make them quicker and more responsive.
  • Base damage increased by 10%.
  • All attacks with charges are now affected by perks that are affecting heavy attacks.
  • Fixed several issues with contested health recovery.
  • Fixed an issue that was causing reduced damage in some cases.
  • Fixed several issues with weapon perks not applying correctly.

🟡Omnissian Axe (Heroic version - Spark of the Omnissiah)

  • Shock zone damage is increased by 100%.

Description Fixes

  • Fixed the menu description of “Tide of Battle” perk for Combat Knife and Power Fist to reflect the correct value.
  • Fixed the menu description of “Ground Shake” perk for Power Fist to reflect the correct value (5 meters).
  • Fixed the menu description of “Crushing Heel” perk for Chainsword to reflect the correct value (40%).

PVE PERKS

Vanguard

  • 🟡 Grapnel Launcher activation now interrupts Melee attacks.
  • Moving Target has been modified: “A Range kill enemy restores Ability Charge by 5%”.
  • Retribution has been reworked: “When Ammo Clip of Ranged Weapon has less than 50% Ammunition, Melee Damage increases by 20%, bonus is now multiplicative”.
  • The damage reduction of Close-Combat Focus has been increased from 20% to 25%.
  • Thrill of the Fight has been moved and is replaced with a new perk, Grapnel Strike: “During a Gun Strike, you fire the Grapnel Launcher instead of your Secondary Weapon, dealing Area Damage and applying Vulnerability.” 🟡 Base damage is increased by 100% for Grapnel Strike Gun Strike.
  • The bonus damage of Melee Champion has been reduced from 15% to 10%, bonus is now multiplicative.
  • Restless Fortitude has been replaced with a new perk, Kinetic Momentum: “After using Grapnel Launcher you deal 20% more Damage for 10 seconds."
  • Tenacity: Cooldown has been reduced from 15 to 10 seconds.
  • Tip of the Spear is now a Prestige Perk and has been replaced with a new perk, Stunning Grapnel: “Holding the Ability charges the Grapnel Launcher. A fully charged Grapnel Launcher Stuns the target but does not propel you towards an enemy. Grapnel Launcher ignores Minoris-level enemies." 🟡 Charge duration is increased from 1 to 2 seconds for Overcharged Tether.
  • Prestige perk Exigency Charge has been replaced with Tip of the Spear.
  • Grim Determination has been replaced with a new perk, Vengeful Kick: “Diving Kick applies Revenge to the target for 8 seconds. Melee attacks against a target affected by Revenge also damage nearby enemies."
  • Combat Readiness has been replaced with a new perk, Taste for Blood: “Performing a Finisher with the Grapnel Launcher increases Ranged Damage by 25% for 10 seconds."
  • Emperor's Blessing has been replaced with a new perk, Vengeful Sidearm: “Ranged Damage from your Secondary Weapon applies Revenge to the target for 8 seconds. Melee attacks against a target affected by Revenge also damage nearby enemies. Cooldown is 30 seconds."
  • Melee Mastery: Melee Damage bonus is now multiplicative.
  • 🟡 Zone of Impact deals 50% reduced damage in a smaller radius if it was a close range Grapnel Launcher usage.

Tactical

  • Improved Efficiency perk bonus increased from 25% to 30%.
  • Mobile Auspex perk duration bonus increased from 4 to 7 seconds.
  • Strong Point perk bonus is now multiplicative, but reduced to 15%.
  • Prime Target perk now also passively buffs gunstrike damage by 20%.

Sniper

  • Fixed menu description of Iron Grip.

CHAOS SIEGE MODE

  • New enemy - Loyalist Tactical Marine
  • Loyalist Heavy Marine health has been decreased from 250 to 230.
  • Loyalist Assault Marine health has been decreased from 250 to 180.
  • Loyalist Sniper Marine health has been decreased from 250 points to 130.

🟡QUALITY OF LIFE

  • Added level lock for Absolute Siege Mode and Absolute Stratagems mode

🟡 TRIALS OF RESOLVE

  • Number of required waves is changed from 25 to 15 for the "Unending Vigil" ordeal.

PVP

  • Adjusted the number and locations of ammo and equipment pickups across all PvP maps.
  • Improved conditions for spawn position swap system.

CUSTOMISATION

  • Heroic Right Pauldron Mark VI Corvus is added for Sniper and Vanguard classes.
  • Space Wolves and Salamanders Champion tabards are added for Vanguard and Heavy classes.
  • Imperial Fists Champion Left Pauldron is added for Vanguard.
  • Iron Hands Champion tabard is added for Vanguard and Heavy classes.
  • Vanguard's Prestige Omni-Scrambler is added for Sniper class.
  • Tactical's Prestige Tabard is added for Assault, Vanguard, Bulwark and Heavy classes.
  • Heavy's Prestige Iron Halo is added for Tactical and Bulwark classes.
  • Bulwark's robes have been separated from the Chest slot and moved to a separate Cloth slot.
  • Cape customisation slot is added for Bulwark with Vermillion, Sable and DLC's Capes.
  • Decals customisation is added to Survivor's and Imperialis Greaves.
  • Lots of emblems have been added to knee decals.
  • Chapter emblems are added for knee decals.
  • Added Mark X Skull Breastplate to the Refinement and Redemption shop.
  • Lots of minor customization fixes.

GENERAL FIXES

  • Fixed an issue where “Able Precision” did not trigger after using a Techmarine Class Ability.
  • Improved parry reliability versus enemies with quick series of attacks (i.e. Tyranid Warrior with a whip).
  • Fixed an issue where the “Slash Momentum” perk did not work with the Frost Axe’s empowered Whirl Slash.
  • Fixed an issue with Power Axe’s perk “Tactical Retreat” granting 25% increased melee damage without requiring a Power Backstep.
  • Fixed an issue where One-Handed Hammer would cause several damage instances instead of one.
  • Fixed an issue where One-Handed Hammer would not deal damage with Underhand Swing.
  • Fixed an issue with Assaut's perk "Furious Strikes" triggering simultaneously with "Commitment" perk at maximum ability charges.
  • Fixed an issue with Heroic Plasma Pistol failing to charge in rare cases.
  • Fixed an issue with Argent Edge no applying Auspex Scan with Battle Focus perk in some cases.
  • Fixed an issue with difficulty damage scaling of Bulwark’s "Emergency Countermeasure" and "Defensive Advantage" perks.
  • Crash fixes and general stability improvements.
  • Lots of minor UI and localisation fixes.

TECH

  • Loading times improvements.
  • Memory optimisations.
  • Minor performance improvements.
  • General connectivity improvements.

items.title: Avengers: Doomsday Teaser Shows Magneto Trying to Rip Doom's Mask Off, Leaves Us With More Questions Than Answers
items.description: Avengers: Doomsday has a new TV spot, shown in the U.S. overnight, that reveals key new scenes involving Magneto, Doom, Steve Rogers, and Thor.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Avengers: Doomsday has a new TV spot, shown in the U.S. overnight, that reveals key new scenes involving Magneto, Doom, Steve Rogers, and Thor.

The highlight of the TV spot, below, is Magneto desperately trying to use his mutant power to rip Doom’s mask off. "He is pain,” Magneto says. “He is extinction.” “I am Doom," Doom adds.

Unfortunately for our heroes, Doom is so powerful that he’s able to force it back on before his — presumably Robert Downey Jr.’s — face is revealed.

New teaser for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’.

In theaters December 18. https://t.co/tJxBj54ozs

— Avengers Updates (@AvengersUpdated) November 26, 2026

But is it actually Robert Downey Jr.’s face underneath the mask? There are all sorts of theories doing the rounds that suggest Marvel may be misdirecting fans about Doom’s true identity in Doomsday. We get a decent look at Doom’s green eyes before he uses his overwhelming power to conceal his face once again. Some are convinced it’s Oppenheimer star Cillian Murphy under the mask. That would be quite the shock given everything we know and have seen about the movie so far.

Earlier this month, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Doomsday. “Is Steve Rogers a Johnny Storm variant?" asked Feige. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom.” Is Feige misdirecting fans here?

Why would Magneto try to rip Doom’s mask off in the first place, rather than, say, immediately crush it? Perhaps the plan here is to remove the mask so that Professor X can get in his head? Either way, it doesn’t work.

We also have a new look at Steve Rogers and Thor calmly walking up to Doom in his lair in Latveria. Are they trying to reason with Doom? Do they mean to confront him about his true motivation after some dramatic discovery? Steve Rogers looks pretty mad in this brief glimpse at the scene. Perhaps he feels betrayed?

And finally, we get the shot of Thor trying to hit Doom with Stormbreaker, only for Doom to block the hit with his finger.

Certainly, the more Marvel shows this movie, the more powerful Doom looks. Thanos was a powerful antagonist for sure, but he wasn’t this powerful. I expect the Avengers, X-Men, and The Fantastic Four are in for a rough ride.

Time for some speculation! Lots of people are suggesting there’s something off about Steve Rogers in what we’ve seen of him so far in this movie, to the point where they’re wondering if it’s actually Loki casting some illusion over everyone. We know Loki goes to see Steve and Peggy in what we now believe is The Fantastic Four’s universe to offer his help. Is this the help he was talking about?

We also see Doom’s three Latverian Witches in the new TV spot. While their identities remain a secret for now, fans believe they could be Sylvie, Clea, and Wanda. Are the masks they wear part of Doom’s magic mind control?

We’ve got plenty more on Avengers: Doomsday, including plans for a special tribute to Patrick Stewart, a first look at Kelsey Grammer's Beast, and fears over Bucky’s fate.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters December 18.

items.title: Rockstar Explains Why it Added Consequences to GTA 6's Violence and Crimes
items.description: Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6.

In an interview with Eurogamer, Nelson was asked about Rockstar's approach to the systems and themes in GTA 6. He said that a lot of it was born out of all of the work they put into Red Dead Redemption 2, specifically having a reactive world that responds to the player's behavior and choices. He explained that there was a desire to evolve the GTA experience and to "give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun.'"

That means players can now point a gun at someone and threaten them, rather than having to beat or kill them to steal their money. The threat of violence is just as prevalent as the violence itself in GTA 6, and it also plays into the morality-adjacent system that is your criminal profile. The game doesn't explicitly punish you for doing bad things, because it's GTA, and you're bound to do bad things. However, it judges you on how harsh you are. If you rob a store with minimal force or only attack people if they draw on you first, attempting to minimize casualties, your profile won't change. If you go in and kill everyone, the level may decrease.

This prompted Rockstar to expand NPC interactions even further. If you drew a gun in GTA 5, no one cared until it was actively pointed at them. Now, people will begin to quietly scurry away if they see you pull a rifle out of your trunk. Nelson explained that while the powerful rampages were fun for a while in previous games, they lacked substance and would get old quickly. In GTA 6, the process to start mowing people down takes a bit more thought because you don't have an endless pocket of weapons anymore.

"You have to call your car," says Nelson. "You have to pop a car trunk and get [a weapon], and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up, and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.

"And then, you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off, and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your criminal profile until it breaks, and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"

The more realistic approach with GTA 6 has been a bit divisive for purists. Some don't want consequences; they want a power fantasy, and GTA 6 is decidely not that. If you want a supercar, it's going to take you dozens of hours before you can steal one. There's a progression to the chaos. For some, that's more rewarding. For others who want that quick fix, it's cumbersome. It'll be interesting to see how Rockstar looks at all of the responses to the game and how that informs the next GTA.

Will they go further down this path or will they try to find a greater middle ground? The game certainly isn't hurting despite some vocal critics. GTA 6 is the highest rated game in history on Metacritic and generated nearly $4 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. IGN gave the game a 10 out of 10, praising it for its depth and detail.

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from our review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

items.title: Spotify Reveals Massive Spike in Streams for Music Featured in GTA 6
items.description: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.

In an email sent to IGN, Spotify revealed that the GTA 6 hype is inspiring listeners to add tons of music from the game to their playlists. In addition to hype for the original music created specifically for the game, such as Justice's Flower in a Hurricane, Carly Rae Jepsen's 2015 song Run Away With Me saw a 940% increase in streams following the game's release. The song plays during a pivotal moment in GTA 6's first chapter and is arguably one of the best sections in the game.

Additionally, fans are listening to the official GTA 6 playlist en masse and are actively searching for things related to the game. You can view the full breakdown courtesy of Spotify below.

  • Following the release of GTA 6, streams of Carly Rae Jepsen's “Run Away With Me” spiked on Nov. 24, increasing by 940% in the U.S. and 1,255% in Canada compared to its average streams.
  • On Nov. 23, “Flower In A Hurricane” by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard hit number 1 on BOTH Spotify’s Daily Top Songs charts globally and in the U.S.
  • Streams of The Official Grand Theft Auto Playlist surged week over week, rising 275% globally and 355% in the U.S. (on Nov. 19 as compared to Nov. 12).
  • GTA had fans searching for more. Searches containing “GTA,” “GTA6/VI” or “Grand Theft Auto” surged about 510% globally and 600% in the U.S. compared with the week prior (Nov. 19 vs. Nov. 12).

GTA 6 has been shattering all kinds of records and setting new trends. The game had the biggest launch in the history of PlayStation and sold nearly $4 billion worth of copies in its first 24 hours, making it the highest-grossing entertainment launch of all time by a significant margin. The game has also set viewership records on platforms like Twitch, led to a massive increase in internet traffic, and so much more.

It's a massive cultural moment that's likely not going to end anytime soon. Not only will this game likely get bigger, but it also has more big events on the horizon. It's also expected to release on PC early next year, and an online mode is also heavily speculated to come in the future.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks, or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips, Chapter 2 Guide and Tips, and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips. items.title: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Reveals That Every Hunger Games Movie Has Initially Been Rated R
items.description: Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he has directed in the series were initially rated R and opened up about the process of making them PG-13.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he directed in the series were initially rated R, prompting clever workarounds when editing them.

On paper, The Hunger Games franchise is tonally very interesting. Although it's a young adult novel series, targeting teenagers, it's about children being forced to fight to the death in a dystopian society. The books don't hold back on the violence, and the films have always had to walk a fine line so they can reach the widest audience possible. The process of making the movies PG-13 is complicated and often inconsistent.

When speaking with Kevin McCarthy, director Francis Lawrence noted that all five of the Hunger Games films he has worked on were initially rated R. The director noted that across his whole career, he has run into an issue of making a movie with a PG-13 rating in mind, but the MPA (Motion Picture Association) reserves the right to give it an R if it's too "intense," even if there's no excessive blood, gore, language, or nudity. It happened with Constantine, it was a concern with I Am Legend, and it has happened regularly with The Hunger Games series.

In one of the Mockingjay films, Lawrence had to cut a scene of a little girl crying and screaming over the body of her dead mother. There wasn't any blood, but the performance was so visceral that it pushed the film closer to an R-rating.

He revealed that the process is somewhat subjective, as the people who rate the movies change, their tastes change, and he was even able to identify specific changes on particular movies.

In regards to Sunrise on the Reaping, he believes that the MPA has become more "conservative" with their judgment of a film, prompting them to tweak the project and show it to the organization four or five times. He also said that sometimes he makes the content more intense on purpose when presenting it to the MPA, so when they edit it, they can show the "intended" version, and it looks more tame by comparison. One example of this is amplifying sound effects to make it sound gnarlier, and then reigning it in on subsequent edits.

Lawrence went on to note that he is surprised by how much these movies can get away with in a PG-13 context, but believes there's a thematic relevance that the MPA accepts.

"It does help that there's been so many of these now that there's [a] precedent," he said. "There's also real thematic relevance to these stories, and I think that also really helps, that in the end they're anti-violence stories. They're about the consequences of violence, the consequences of war; they're really about themes that are educating people. I do think the MPA takes that into consideration when they look at sequences that are intense. They have different emotional values, and it's not really splattercore, in a way.

"But I definitely do intensify beyond a limit of where I think it will be accepted as PG-13 purposely, because I know we are going to have to pull back on certain things."

He explained that certain deaths were more brutal and gratuitous in initial cuts of the film, but ultimately had to be adjusted for a PG-13 rating.

"One thing I really wanted to keep was we had a very specific neck wound on Maysilee in her death. Basically the one that kills her is right here," said Lawrence while pointing at the center of his neck. "And he's covering it and when his hand comes off, you can see blood starting to drip out of it, and you can see the hole, and it's why she can't speak. And they made us get rid of that, and that's what killed me."

The Hunger Games films are far from the only big mainstream action movies that have to get creative with how they depict violence. items.title: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
items.description: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.

If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects.

This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3.) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother.

Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations.

“FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote. “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…”

That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.”

“Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied.

GTA 6 is a game like no other. Its world is so massive and detailed that some players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of chilling out in Key Lento and diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and playing billiards at the Rusty Anchor. And we can’t blame them; there’s tons of stuff to do, even in Chapter 1.

items.title: LEGO Announces 4 New Sets Based on the Harry Potter HBO Series
items.author: Chris Reed
items.content:
The LEGO Harry Potter theme has been a mainstay since the first set came out in 2001. Now that HBO has a new TV adaptation of the Wizarding World in the works (set to debut on December 25), LEGO has finally unveiled a new batch of sets based on the new series. Four new sets have been announced, two of which are available to preorder now. They're all out January 1. Let’s take a look.

Featured in this article

The four sets offer a nice selection of characters and locations from the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which is what the HBO show’s first season adapts.

Honestly, these sets don’t look all that distinct from the sets based on the movies. Then again, based on the TV show’s trailer, they didn’t really change much when adapting the franchise into a show.

LEGO Harry Potter: Privet Drive

  • Preorder at LEGO

It all starts on 4 Privet Drive. That’s where we find the home of the Dursley family, who adopt Harry Potter after you-know-who kills his parents. The Dursleys aren’t very nice to Harry, but this LEGO set lets you build their two-story house, complete with Harry’s cupboard under the stairs. This one’s available for preorder now.

LEGO Harry Potter: Gryffindor Common Room

  • Preorder at LEGO

The three main young wizards all end up in house Gryffindor, so they spend a lot of time in the common room. This set recreates that cozy space, complete with a fireplace, five minifigures, and a Quidditch table that’s unique to the show.

LEGO Harry Potter: Hogwarts Express & Platform 9¾

  • Not available for preorder

There are so many now-iconic things in the first book that it must have been hard to pick what to base sets on. That said, it would be a shame if there wasn’t a new Hogwarts Express set. This set has platform 9¾, plus the bold red train. It also includes minifigures for Harry, Hermione, Ron, Draco Malfoy, and Molly Weasley — all characters that appear in or around the train in the book.

LEGO BrickHeadz: Harry, Draco and Hagrid Figures

  • Not available for preorder

BrickHeadz are kind of like LEGO’s take on Funko Pops. They depict known characters from pop culture, but in a stylized design, and they’re meant for display. These seem like good, blocky renditions of the trio they depict.

For more, check out all the best LEGO Black Friday deals available now. And take a gander at our running list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

items.title: 'People Are Doing It Too Quickly Now' — The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Speaks Out on YA Franchise Reboots
items.description: I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.

Francis Lawrence has directed all but one movie in The Hunger Games series. He’s been with the franchise for over a decade; the first film, directed by Gary Ross, released in 2012, after which Lawrence took up the mantle for all subsequent movies.

It’s one of several iconic movie franchises that defined the YA boom of the 2000s - mid-2010s. And unlike other series from this time period, it has neither languished nor suffered a reboot before its corpse is even cold.

HBO’s forthcoming Harry Potter series is perhaps the most egregious example of such a reboot. The last Harry Potter movie released in 2011, and its cast defined an entire generation of fans who grew up watching their adventures at Hogwarts. It seems almost insulting to reimagine the world that was so painstakingly built over the course of a decade — but that’s just my opinion.

I’m not alone in this line of thinking, though. When asked about his feelings on reboots, Lawrence agreed that they’re happening too soon, bringing up Warner Bros.’ thankfully canceled idea for an I Am Legend reboot in 2014, just seven years after the original film was released.

“I mean, I do feel like people are doing it sort of too quickly now,” he mused. “I agree with you on that. People started talking about that with I Am Legend. I don't remember how long ago, but it felt like 10 years had gone by or something, and somebody was thinking of remaking it already at Warner. I'm like, ‘Really? 10 years, that's it?’”

Given the imminent release of HBO’s Harry Potter series on Christmas day, I had to bring up the very real possibility that The Hunger Games sees a reboot in the next decade or so — an idea that Lawrence wasn’t sure would get Suzanne Collins’ blessing.

“I don't know how I would feel about it,” he admitted. “I also don't know if Suzanne has anything in place to sort of protect against that, but that'd be really, really interesting to figure out. But I think it's a tough one. I mean, if Suzanne backed it, I think some spinoffs, and obviously if she writes other books, things like that could be interesting, as long as she backs it and comes up with it and has the thematic reasonings and philosophies that she usually does, that would be cool. But I don't know how you go back and remake the original movies and it not be [Jennifer Lawrence]."

To his point, The Hunger Games franchise has managed to stay in the public consciousness, owing in part to its later release during the YA boom (the final film in the original series came out in 2015) and its two prequel movies that rocked theaters in the 2020s. The latest movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, received solid reviews from critics, earning an 8 out of 10 from IGN.

For more news on this newest entry in The Hunger Games series, check out my interview with star Joseph Zada, who told me all about how he managed to pull off Woody Harrelson's unmistakable accent, and whether or not the cast is Team Peeta or Team Gale.

items.title: GTA 6 Doesn't Let You Replay Missions, and Rockstar Says There's a Good Reason for That
items.description: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.

When speaking with Kotaku, Rockstar Games senior design director Scott Butchard explained why the studio scrapped a mission replay menu in GTA 6. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 allowed players to freely replay missions, but that's not the case in GTA 6. According to Butchard, they considered bringing the feature back, but cut it because it was "at odds" with the story.

“Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.”

The lack of a mission replay option has been a point of contention for fans. GTA 6 has some of the best missions in the franchise, particularly the final mission of Chapter 1. Given that GTA 6 can take players anywhere from 50 - 100 hours to finish, most people probably won't start the entire game over just to re-experience their favorite mission. However, it's worth noting that Butchard says the game doesn't "currently support" this feature. Maybe it'll come in the form of an update later, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed that.

GTA 6's story and missions can deviate somewhat significantly based on your choices. Certain characters can be killed or spared, objectives can be completed in different ways, and the entire relationship between Jason and Lucia can vary based on your actions. You can get entirely different dialogue options and cutscenes based on these differences, which might be why a mission replay system isn't as straightforward as it was previous games.

However, Red Dead Redemption 2 also featured different choices that changed Arthur's character. It wasn't quite as nuanced as GTA 6's variations, though. Maybe Rockstar will figure out a way to do this, but it clearly fell low on the priority list, if it was on the list at all by the end of development. Even if Rockstar never adds it, modders will probably find a way to slot it in when the inevitable PC version releases.

items.title: 'It Would Be Absolutely Incredible' — Hideki Kamiya Wants to Make a New Castlevania Game With Konami
items.description: Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Okami, wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something “absolutely incredible.”
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Okami, wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something "absolutely incredible" alongside Konami.

Hideki Kamiya is back in the saddle at CLOVERS, his independent game studio made up of former CLOVER staff who are currently hard at work on the Okami sequel. He made the company’s independent status extremely clear in his latest YouTube video, reminding excited fans to stop asking him about Capcom-owned franchises (or even sequels to games like God Hand, since he had no part in its development).

Given CLOVERS’ status as an independent company that’s already working with a major developer in Capcom, Kamiya floated ideas for future collaborations with other big developers once the Okami sequel is out in the world. One of those ideas was a partnership with Konami for a Castlevania game, which he promised would be “incredible,” if it actually ends up happening.

“Since we’re independent and don’t have any outside funding, we want to stay on good terms — or rather, collaborate — with various companies and keep doing interesting things,” he explained. “Of course, I want to keep building a good relationship with Capcom, and naturally, I’d like to be on good terms with Nintendo, too.

“...Maybe I could make a new Getsufumaden with Konami. Oh, and Castlevania. If we made it, it would be absolutely incredible, so please, let us take the job. I am a bit busy right now, though,” he laughed.

A Castlevania game from a mind like Kamiya’s would definitely be something special. Would it be a 3D action game like Bayonetta, or more of a 2D side-scroller in the vein of Viewtiful Joe? The possibilities are endless, and given that Konami is already on a mission to revitalize its classic IPs with new games, the possibility of a team-up with CLOVERS on a Castlevania title isn’t totally out of the question.

It's also worth noting that the Castlevania franchise enjoyed a new installment in Belmont's Curse late last month. Alongside its animated adaptations on Netflix, Konami's classic vampire-slaying game series is getting a second wind, and Kamiya would like to be part of that, though whether or not this actually happens remains to be seen.
